chapter: Learning the trombone and jam sessions
title: Influences: the Jenkins band trombonists and Louis Armstrong
summary: His uncle did not influence him; the Jenkins Orphan Band did, and then Louis Armstrong; the Jenkins boys were about 13 to 18.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: I saw in Chilton's book that you had an uncle who played trombone in Jim Europe's band. Was he any kind of an influence on you, or did he have anything to do with your--

No, he didn't have any. He played but he didn't influence me. Who influenced me for trombone was these guys in the Jenkin's Orphan Band. They were the guys who really influenced me because I'd watched them. In fact, I think I liked the way they walked, you know. That was the first thing. And they's slide those horns all out--. They had a lot of color with what they were doing and this influenced me an awful lot.

And besides the fact that I liked the sound of the trombone. I don't think -- I didn't think I could ever learn the trumpet. It just seemed much harder to me, you know, at that time being a kid, you know. But I wanted to play trumpet first but it just seemed so hard to me. And then after I heard Louis play, from then on I said I don't think I could ever do that, you know. And he was playing so good so far back there then, you know. He was amazing because he was so far ahead of his time.
And after I had heard all the other trumpet players in Jenkin's Orphan Bandand all, then finally I heard Louis. And well, this was the epitome to me -- I think to almost all
musicians back in the '20's. Louis was just it, you know.
Was the Jenkins Orphan Band very, very young players, or were they --
Yeah, they were young. They were young boys.
But they were still like minors --
Oh, yeah. But they could play because --
How old -- from what age range --

I think -- I think they ranged from about 13 to about -- 13 or 14 to about 18. I think they were about in that bracket, you know. But they were always training younger ones to come up, you know. They were very young.
